questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook tasty dishes with garlic and salt
The history of Halloween festivals in Ireland
Superstitions and traditions connected with food
Why eggs are a healthy choice for lunch
questions.why: Sam says many superstitions are connected to food, as they'll discover in the programme.

questions.q: Why does Rob tell Sam to throw salt over his shoulder?
options: Because spilling salt is thought to be bad luck
Because there is too much salt on the egg
To clean the floor
To make a wish for his birthday
questions.why: Rob says, 'It's bad luck to spill salt!'

questions.q: What does Sam realise after Rob's questions about birthdays and weddings?
options: He has never been to a wedding
Rob is not superstitious at all
Superstitions are only for children
He may be more superstitious than he thought
questions.why: Sam says yes to both and adds, 'Maybe I'm more superstitious than I thought!'

questions.q: According to Tasha Marks, what else is garlic believed to protect against?
options: Colds, coughs and flu in the winter
The 'evil eye', or bad luck in general
Evil spirits and ghosts at Halloween
Bad dreams and trouble sleeping
questions.why: She says garlic has also been thought to ward off the 'evil eye', a term for any bad luck.

questions.q: What point does Sam make about food superstitions after hearing Tasha Marks?
options: They are all based on science
They are slowly dying out around the world
They also give our lives meaning
They only exist in Europe
questions.why: Sam says food superstitions aren't only about bad luck – they also give our lives meaning.

options: She writes books about the history of food
She shows tourists local food traditions
She is a chef in a famous restaurant
She presents The Food Chain
questions.why: She owns a tourist agency in Hyderabad, introducing visitors to the city's food traditions.

questions.q: When is the special chutney given, according to Jonty?
options: On 1st January
At weddings
On birthdays
At Hindu New Year
questions.why: She says it's given at the Hindu calendar New Year, not 1st January.

questions.q: What does the chutney's mix of tastes represent?
options: The good and bad parts of the coming year
The different regions and cultures of India
The family's favourite foods
A wish for a sweet life only
questions.why: Her mum said the year would have happiness, challenges, sadness and bitterness, like the chutney.
